portion_doctrine: POSING 101 OG segments 1-10: A high-quality transcript corpus spanning 7 distinct instructional sources on posing techniques for portrait photography. Includes foundational posing theory (Tim Shields' recipe methodology), gender-specific approaches (Sal Cincotta for women, professional male posing frameworks), advanced techniques (facial expressions, angles, emotional depth), practical non-model coaching (Omar Gonzalez), self-portrait shooting, and comprehensive pose documentation. Core insight: posing is not demonized instruction but the photographer's responsibility to bring out the subject's best form across all body types and contexts.

foundational_recipes: Rule of thirds: place subject left/right third, face on top third line, avoid center framing
Background management: no protruding elements behind head (telephone poles, trees), blurring via aperture priority + small f-stop + zoom + focus on face
Lighting setup: avoid backlit scenarios (sunset behind subject), use key light + fill light model, natural light via window with diffusing bedsheet, or artificial lights
Portrait recipe: (1) Move subject using rule of thirds, (2) Frame interesting background elements on third lines, (3) Ensure correct lighting on subject not backlit

female_posing: Chin positioning: 'turtle' technique - extend neck by moving chin forward/down to elongate face and eliminate double chin
Hip angle: push hip to rear (not to camera) to thin the body; push to camera adds weight
S-curve body: ankles together, lift right foot heel, collapse that knee inward to create thinner silhouette; turn hip away from camera subtly
Arms: gap between arm and body needed; pull elbow back to thin arms and lead eye along curves; avoid pressing arms flat to body
Asymmetry mandatory: drop one shoulder more than other, avoid perfectly symmetrical stance (cheery, not elegant)
Hands: vary placement - pockets, resting, gripping fabric - avoid showing full palm square to camera
Distance between body parts: maintain gaps between limbs and torso to show shape; compress body vertically where needed
Avoid similarity: do not mirror same pose with both hands/legs; create variation
Golden angle: each person has an optimal facial profile angle; test multiple angles to find the one that best lights expression and bone structure
Hair styling: maintain consistency or vary systematically by angle; poor hair kills an otherwise perfect pose
Camera direction: direct gaze vs. off-camera gaze both valid; pair with body rotation (e.g., shoulders one way, eyes another)
Expressions: cool/magazine smolder, soft/painting gentle, fun/laughing authentic - three tiers to cycle
Tall vs. short clients: tall clients benefit from full-body shots; shorter clients thrive in halves/crops; avoid comparing scales within single frame
male_posing: Hand management: hands in or out of pockets (thumbs IN, never pointing out like 'two little penises'), avoid framing the crotch
One hand active, one passive: if hand in pocket, other hand holds jacket, adjusts watch, or props cuff; prevents feminine over-posing
Arm extension: create gap between arm and body (elbows out slightly) to broaden shoulders; fists under biceps if arms are small
Body angle: turn toward light source (not away like female form) to create V-shape, appear bigger/broader; slouch glorified (concave chest forward, shoulders back)
Feet setup: feet shoulder-width or closer, bend front knee slightly, weight on back leg, never 'pigeon toe'
Lean forward posture: chest and shoulders toward camera, gut further away (concave upper body creates valleys and peaks)
Chin tuck: do turtle movement if plus-sized or double chin risk; chin forward with lean-back body position creates shortening effect
Avoid feminine angles: turning body away from light, chin to outer shoulder, over-posing makes male subjects look feminine
Posture hierarchy: strong shoulders (down/braced), good spinal alignment, feet shoulder-width spacing, elongate limbs by extending

seven_posing_points: Feet/ankles: together, shoulder-width, wider stance; rotate 360, twist top body independently
Knees: tippy-toe (activates), bend in/out, cross over, different spread widths change body silhouette
Hips: push forward vs. back vs. side angles; rotation independent of legs; creates S-curve when paired with leg bend
Torso/chest: lean forward/back, twist sideways, create concave upper body for male form
Shoulders: drop one more than other (asymmetry), shrug up then release, roll back to open chest, broaden via arm positioning
Head/face: multiple tilt angles (up, down, side, forward), chin positioning, jaw extension
Eyes: gaze direction (camera, over shoulder, ground, off-camera), eye level changes with head tilt and camera angle
practical_shooting_strategies: Pre-shoot orientation with non-models: warm-up, show poses via demo (subject becomes photographer), teach mirror copying, assess shyness level
Burst shooting + motion: have subjects walk, skip, jump to break set poses and catch genuine expressions after movement
Variety at one location: work three expression levels (cool/smolder, soft/gentle, fun/authentic), vary shoulders/head/eyes independently, change focal length (wide to tight to headshot)
Rotation principle: if stuck on pose ideas, rotate subject slightly on same pose (creates new look instantly)
Story-based sequencing: build 15+ distinct poses from single narrative arc (e.g., couple's story from dance to proposal to bike ride = multiple distinct frames from one scene)
Avoid dead/stiff expressions: have subjects look off-camera or to side; direct gaze requires present expression/energy

short_people: Low angles always (shoot up from below to make height appear greater)
Half-body crop preferred (avoid full-body which shows proportion gaps)
Avoid props with scale (bikes, cars) that emphasize size difference
High or eye-level camera angles only; never shoot from above
Use background elements for height perception (walls, blank backgrounds show no scale comparison)
thin_people: Avoid: full frontal square stance, side-profile single-angle, low angles (accentuate thinness)
Do: half-body crops, face-forward square poses, eye-level or slightly high angles
Layer clothing (t-shirt under jacket, different textures), use accessories (belts, watches, glasses)
Material support: bring guitar, prop with object, sit on chair with hand placement for body structure
Create negative space triangles: arm angles, leg spacing, object placement create visual bulk
plus_size_people: Object blocking: partial obscuring behind props, objects in frame (tree, fence), hands carrying things
Half-body framing with amazing expressions (happiness, laughter, movement) > visible body shape
Avoid supporting angles: never shoot straight at torso square; always 45-degree angle or more rotated
High-emotion posing: action poses (dancing, moving) distract from shape; joy reads stronger than body awareness
Lighting + shadow: side lighting creates shadow for contour; diffused light reduces highlighting
Clothing fit: ensure clothes fit properly (loose vs. tailored changes silhouette dramatically)

angle_systems: Face angles: 9-12 distinct chin positions (center, side, up, down, diagonal, tilted) create different feelings/expressions
Camera angles: looking down from above = power/doubt, looking up from below = admiration/serving; neither better, convey different emotional content
Deliberate foreshortening: compression of body parts (hand pointing at camera is short, but extended arm is long) used to hide or emphasize
Multiple tilts: not just up/down but forward tilt, side tilt, combinations exponentially increase variation
emotional_expression: Inner diversity concept: challenge own limiting beliefs about attractiveness (you contain all versions: sexy, cool, sensual, etc.)
Emotional stretch posing: paired with physical stretch (hand across chest, shoulder rotation) to access emotional depth
Hands-on direction: small isolated motions (rotate to me, step back walk through, dancer hip isolation) one action at a time
Contrast between body and face: body one direction, eyes/face another creates tension and visual interest
Connecting chin to shoulder: advanced technique for tight frames; creates feminine energy when executed
professional_workflow: Test shots first: move around, cross legs, cross arms, look away, look at camera, vary continuously
Never stop moving: continuous motion = better candid moments than static poses
Hands-on positioning: hide hands in pockets/behind back during clicking to avoid awkward resting position
Wardrobe as pose tool: layers, jackets, belts, accessories provide hand placement options and visual variety
Selection process: critical skill - choose photos with best lighting, posing, expression (subjects often pick worst photos)
Editing layers: portrait faces = retouch/brighten, scenic = environment enhancement; different layers for different needs

tools_and_tech: Bluetooth remote clicker (essential for solo self-portrait work)
Tripod minimum 6 ft tall (allows full-body shots)
Portrait mode on phone (creates depth blur, cinematic look)
FaceApp (AI retouching, preset filters, subtle enhancement)
Rule of thirds grid overlay (compositional aid)
Camera settings: aperture priority mode, smallest f-stop possible (f/2.8, f/1.4), zoom lens to maximum, focus on face/eyes
contradictions_noted: Thin people should avoid side-profile but also need angle variation - resolution: vary angles via head tilt/expression, not pure profile rotation
Symmetry demonized for women but necessary symmetry for baseline posture - resolution: asymmetric arm/leg placement over asymmetric core structure
Over-posing makes men look feminine but requires intentional posing - resolution: posing is framework; excess emotionality/movement makes masculine pose read feminine, not pose itself
Different frame sizes (full-body, half, close-up) required but short subjects limited to specific frames - resolution: use framing + lighting + angle to work within constraints

operating_rules: Posing is not a dirty word; it brings out the best in subjects - establish this mindset with clients
Photographer bears responsibility for subject looking good, not the subject
Every body type has different optimal posing angles - no universal 'best angle'
Rotation on any existing pose creates new variation instantly (critical efficiency principle)
Movement before stillness: have subjects walk/jump/move first, then freeze in best moment
One location, three expression levels, multiple focal lengths = extract maximum diversity from minimal setup
Body language communicates before face; establish posture/positioning before worrying about expression
Hands are most expressive after eyes - give them deliberate jobs (pockets, props, gripping)
Gaps and negative space create flattering silhouettes more than poses alone
Emotion/expression overrides body visibility for plus-size subjects (joy > shape awareness)
prompts_for_future_use: Walk me through your 'golden angle' using the 9-12 chin positions technique
Show me how rotation creates pose variation from a single starting position
Demonstrate the difference between the V-shape (male) and S-curve (female) posture setup
Explain how to extract 15+ distinct poses from a single couple's narrative arc
Describe the three expression tiers and when to deploy each
Walk through the seven posing points from feet to eyes
How does camera angle (looking up vs. down) change emotional reading of pose?
Show the turtle chin technique and when it applies to male subjects
Explain the 'gap between body parts' principle and why it matters for plus-size framing
How do you coach non-models to mirror you effectively without pre-shoot instruction?
skills_referenced: Non-model comfort + direction (verbal coaching without demonizing posing)
Rotation principle (pose multiplication without new concepts)
Deliberate foreshortening for body part emphasis/de-emphasis
Emotional anchoring (inner diversity concept, accessing emotional depth)
Technical self-portrait workflow (tripod + clicker + location scouting + timing)
Selection + editing literacy (choosing best frames, layer-based retouching)
gates_to_apply_before_deployment: Not all poses work for all body types - verify body-type-specific constraints before shooting
Client comfort > perfect posing - assess shyness, adjust intensity accordingly
Lighting constraints change optimal angles - evaluate light source before directing poses
Frame size (full/half/close-up) limits which poses read well - lock framing before pose complexity
Story coherence required - poses should chain logically if building narrative sequence
Expression matching posture - stiff posture + relaxed face or vice versa creates visual dissonance
weird_gold: Tiny isolated motions (one body part at a time) prevent awkward shapes during pose transitions
Hand-in-pocket thumb position changes completely different psychological reads (thumbs IN = formal, thumbs OUT = crude)
Calling male posing 'glorified slouch' reframes lean-forward posture from weakness to intentional V-shape strength
Deliberate foreshortening (compression of body parts in frame) paradoxically makes people look better by hiding proportions
Story-based pose sequencing (extracting 15 poses from one couple narrative) is more time-efficient and cohesive than pose-shopping
Asking non-models to mirror you mirrors their natural rapport (breaks formal photography taboo, creates psychological permission to move)
Camera angle psychology (looking down = doubt, looking up = admiration) changes entire emotional reading without changing pose
Inner diversity concept ('you contain all versions: sexy, cool, sensual') reframes posing as identity exploration not performance
Lip positioning (thumbs in or out, four fingers visible) has disproportionate impact on entire frame read
Burst shooting after high-energy movement (skipping, jumping) captures genuine expressions without forced smiling
contradictions: Rotation is presented as infinite variation principle, but human flexibility limits how far rotation can go without looking unnatural
Seven posing points treated as independent but all interconnected (knee bend affects hip line, which affects shoulder angle)
Non-models coached via mirroring but many subjects have poor body awareness and can't replicate what they're mirroring
Emotion > body visibility for plus-size framing, but authentic emotion is hard to command on set (requires real laughter/movement)
Golden angle universally important but camera angle changes what angle reads as golden for same face
Story-building 15-pose methodology efficient for couples but impractical for fast commercial headshots
Male posing emphasizes 'not feminine' but some feminine poses actually read attractive on male subjects depending on context/vibe
content_ideas: Side-by-side pose comparison: before/after for each body type using same location, showing 3-5 key differences
Rotation principle masterclass: single starting pose, 6-8 rotational variations, numbered frame-by-frame
Story-sequence builder: couple narrative broken into 15 distinct visual moments with pose callouts
Non-model coaching video: actual pre-shoot assessment (shyness evaluation), mirror-teaching, warm-up sequence
Golden angle finder: single subject shot from 12+ angles with annotations of which reads best and why
Seven posing points animated: each joint isolated, demonstrating full range, then combinations
Gender comparison reel: identical location, side-by-side male/female pose strategy differences
Emotion tier breakdown: same pose, three expression intensities (cool, soft, fun) with coaching cues
Self-portrait solo setup: location scouting via TikTok, equipment unboxing, full shoot-to-edit workflow
Body-type posing cheat sheet: plus-size, thin, short, tall as reference cards with do/don't examples
